findings.title: Duplicate `self.downsize` method definition silently overrides the width/height variant
findings.body: Two class methods named `downsize` are defined: one accepting `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (line 145) and a second accepting `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (line 149). Ruby allows method redefinition, so the second definition completely replaces the first — the width/height variant becomes dead code and unreachable. Any existing caller elsewhere in the codebase that still invokes `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, width, height, opts)` with 5 positional arguments will now raise an ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments) because the active method only accepts 3 positional args plus an options hash. This is an undocumented, breaking change to the public API of `OptimizedImage.downsize` and the first definition should be removed or the overload properly consolidated.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB download cap ignores SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb
findings.body: The API URL-download path now uses a hardcoded `10.megabytes` limit instead of the configurable `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` that was previously used. This removes admin control over the maximum download size for API-sourced uploads (both images and non-image attachments go through this code path), and is inconsistent with the newly-added downsizing logic a few lines below that still reads `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` to decide when to shrink an image. Admins who configure a smaller max image/attachment size will no longer have that limit enforced for URL-based uploads.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB client-side file size limit ignores per-type SiteSettings
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` previously computed `maxSizeKB` from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, allowing separate configurable limits for images vs attachments. It now hardcodes `10 * 1024` KB for all upload types, so admin-configured `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb` settings are no longer respected client-side. This creates an inconsistency with server-side logic (uploads_controller.rb) which still consults `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, and silently changes the enforced limit for attachments regardless of what the admin configured.

findings.title: 413 error handler reports a hardcoded 10MB limit instead of the configured value
findings.body: In `displayErrorForUpload`, the 413 (entity too large) handler now hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` instead of reading `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. The error message shown to the user will state an incorrect maximum size whenever the site is configured with a different `max_image_size_kb` value, misleading users about the actual upload limit.

findings.title: No test coverage for the new automatic image downsizing feature
findings.body: The PR adds a non-trivial feature — automatically downsizing images larger than `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` by iteratively calling `OptimizedImage.downsize` up to 5 times — but no tests were added or updated for `uploads_controller.rb` or `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` to verify this logic (e.g., that it stops once the file is small enough, that it gives up after 5 attempts, that it uses the correct dimensions string, or that non-image uploads/API-only cases work as expected). Given the signature changes to `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` and the new retry loop, this is a risky area to leave untested.

findings.title: In-place downsizing with identical from/to path risks data corruption and silent oversized uploads
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` uses the same path for both source and destination. For animated GIFs this is routed to `gifsicle --output <path>` with the same input and output path (see `resize_instructions_animated`/`downsize_instructions_animated` in optimized_image.rb); depending on how gifsicle buffers input before writing, this can truncate/corrupt the source file while it is still being read. Additionally, if `OptimizedImage.downsize` fails (returns false, e.g., ImageMagick/gifsicle missing or erroring) the loop still decrements `attempt` without any error reported to the user, and if the file is still over the limit after 5 attempts, the upload proceeds silently with the oversized file instead of surfacing an error to the caller.
